chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Indeed, my father asked your grandfather about completing the Quran every night.' So your grandfather said to him, 'Every night?' He said to him, 'In the month of Ramadan.' So your grandfather said to him, 'In the month of Ramadan?' My father said to him, 'Yes, as much as I am able.'

So my father used to complete it, forty completions in the month of Ramadan. Then I completed it after my father; sometimes I would add and sometimes I would be deficient, according to my free time, my busyness, my energy, and my laziness.

So when it was the Day of Fitr, I would designate one completion for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), another for Ali (peace be upon him), another for Fatima (peace be upon her), then for the Imams (peace be upon them) until I reached you, so I designated one for you since I entered this state. So what is for me because of that?
He said, 'For you, because of that, is that you will be with them on the Day of Judgment.' I said, 'Allah is the Greatest! So for me is that?' He said, 'Yes,' three times.

key_terms.خَتْمُ الْقُرْآنِ: Completing the recitation of the entire Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for dedicating Quran completions to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia tradition of *khatm al-Qur'an* (completing the Quran) with a specific emphasis on *tawassul* (seeking nearness) by dedicating recitations to the Ahl al-Bayt. The narrator’s practice of varying the number of completions based on capacity reflects the scholarly view that consistency and intention matter more than rigid quantity, while the final dedication to the Imam underscores the spiritual bond between the believer and the living Imam. The Imam’s confirmation that the reward is 'being with them on the Day of Judgment' elevates this act from mere ritual to a means of eschatological proximity to the Prophet and the Imams.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balad, from his father, from Ali Bin Al Mugheira, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My father asked your<sup>asws</sup> grandfather<sup>asws</sup> about completing the (whole) Quran during every night. So your<sup>asws</sup> grandfather<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Every night?’ So he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘In a Month of Ramazan’. So your<sup>asws</sup> grandfather<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘In a Month of Ramazan?’ So my father said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Yes, whatever capacity (I have)’.

It was so that my father used to complete it, forty completions in a Month of Ramazan. Then I was completing it after my father. So sometimes I would exceed and sometimes I would be deficient, based upon a measurement of my free time, and my occupation, and my activity and my laziness.

So whenever it was the day of (Eid) Al-Fitr, I would make one completion to be for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and another one for Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and another for Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup>, then another for the Imams<sup>asws</sup> until I would end up with you<sup>asws</sup>. Thus, I have rendered one (completion) to be for you<sup>asws</sup> since I came to be in this state. So which thing would be for me due to that?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For you, due to that, is that you would happen to be with them<sup>asws</sup> on the Day of Judgment’. I said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest! So, for me would be that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’, three times’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad from his father from Ali ibn al- Mughirah who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu al-Hassan (a.s.) ‘My father once asked your grandfather about reading all of the Holy Quran in one night.’ ‘(Do you mean it to happen) every night?’ Your grandfather inquired. ‘Yes, in the month of Ramadan.’ My father replied. Your grandfather asked him, ‘In the month of Ramadan?’ My father said, ‘Yes, in the month of Ramadan if I could. ’

My father would read the Holy Quran forty times in the whole month of Ramadan. After my father I would read the Holy Quran sometimes more and sometimes less than he did, as I would get a chance within my work, activities and laziness.

On ’id day (after the month of Ramadan) I would assign the reward for reading the Holy Quran once for the Holy prophet, one for Imam Ali, one for Al-Sayyidah Fatimah and one for each Imam until yourself and I assigned the reward for reciting the Holy Quran once for you from the time I am doing this. Will there be anything for me in this?
The Imam said, ‘On the Day of Judgment, you will be with them.’ ‘Allah is greater than can be described, this much for me!’ I exclaimed. The Imam (a.s.) said three times, ‘Yes.’”
